summary: Petroglyphs and inscriptions at Jubbah and Shuwaymis record human and animal imagery across major environmental changes and roughly 10,000 years of history.
Hegra preserves 111 monumental tombs, 94 decorated, along with inscriptions and water wells; UNESCO identifies it as the largest conserved Nabataean site south of Petra.
Mecca and Medina became central places in Muslim religious life, while pilgrimage routes connected western Arabia with communities across Africa and Asia.
status: introductory synthesis; deepen with primary and scholarly sources

summary: At-Turaif in Diriyah preserves a major Najdi architectural and urban ensemble and later became the political centre of the first Saudi state.
The modern Saudi state commemorates 1727 as the beginning of Imam Muhammad bin Saud's rule and the First Saudi State.
status: official state chronology; compare with historiography using 1744 for the alliance milestone

summary: Earlier scholarship commonly uses 1744 for the alliance between Muhammad bin Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab as a major state-forming milestone.
status: historiographic convention; distinguish event dated from 1727 official chronology

topic: End of the First Saudi State
summary: Diriyah was captured after the Egyptian-Ottoman campaign, ending the First Saudi State.
status: introductory synthesis; corroborate with specialist scholarship

summary: A Saudi polity centred on Riyadh was re-established under Turki bin Abdullah in 1824 and lasted, with internal conflict and changing power, until 1891.
Abdulaziz ibn Saud recaptured Riyadh, beginning the political and military consolidation that led to the modern kingdom.
status: widely documented milestone; compare official and independent histories

topic: Proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: The unified state took the name Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, effective 23 September 1932.
Commercial oil production accelerated changes in state finance, infrastructure, urbanization, employment, education and international relations.
status: introductory synthesis; use dated sector data for detailed claims

summary: Saudi Arabia launched Vision 2030 as a national program of economic diversification and social and cultural development. Research should separate announced goals from implemented actions and measured outcomes.
status: current-policy framework; requires dated sources for outcomes
